reader.requirement: On a relative-file DELETE, END-DELETE must terminate the most recently preceding unterminated DELETE (§1985:IV.6.4.3), so statements after it lie outside its INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY phrases, a DELETE ... END-DELETE nests as an imperative statement, a DELETE with no phrase (sequential access) may carry END-DELETE, and a stray END-DELETE is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: END-DELETE reserved at each edition (row reserved true at 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023)

reader.edition-search: deleteStatement ends in conditionalPhrases END_DELETE? with no predicate; its only edition-gated part is the 2002 retryPhrase (VersionConformancePass.VisitRetryPhrase), which is not on the scope path
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f21_02 covers a random-access DELETE inside IF with INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY and END-DELETE; DELETE nested in DELETE, END-DELETE on a sequential-access DELETE with no phrase, implicit termination by ELSE and the stray END-DELETE refusal are not exercised

reader.notes: The record DELETE is the shared grammar rule deleteStatement (the seed KeyedIoBinder.BindDeleteFile is the 2002 DELETE FILE statement, not this one; the record DELETE binds in KeyedIoBinder.BindDelete). Nested, phrase-less and implicitly terminated forms behave as §1985:IV.6.4.3 states and a stray END-DELETE draws COBOL0306.
